book_meta.subtitle_child: My First Nepali IPA Sound Book

ipa_key.name: Tied Denti-Alveolar Affricate
ipa_key.kid_desc: Start with your tongue tip stopping the air behind your top teeth, then slide straight into a crisp 'ts' bee-buzz hiss!
ipa_key.parent_desc: The tie-bar above /t͡s/ links /t/ (denti-alveolar stop closure) and /s/ (sibilant release) into one single Nepali affricate sound.

ipa_key.name: Aspiration (Mahaprana)
ipa_key.kid_desc: Blow a strong gust of mountain wind out of your mouth right as the sound pops!
ipa_key.parent_desc: Superscript [ʰ] marks a strong voiceless burst of air immediately following the release of the affricate.

ipa_key.name: Dental Stop
ipa_key.kid_desc: Press the flat tip of your tongue gently against the back of your top front teeth.
ipa_key.parent_desc: The bridge diacritic beneath /t̪/ means the tongue tip touches the upper front teeth, unlike English alveolar /t/.

ipa_key.name: Open Central Vowel
ipa_key.kid_desc: Open your mouth wide like a yawn and say a bright 'aaah'!
ipa_key.parent_desc: An open central unrounded vowel (आ / ा), fuller and more open than the inherent mid vowel अ (/ʌ/).

sound_recipe.label: 1. Tongue Tip Seal
sound_recipe.detail: Press your tongue tip right behind the upper front teeth to block the air completely.

sound_recipe.label: 2. Tied Hissing Release
sound_recipe.detail: Release the seal into a crisp 'ts' sibilant groove (linked by the top tie-bar).

sound_recipe.label: 3. Big Wind Burst
sound_recipe.detail: Push a strong puff of breath out together with the 'ts' release!

articulation.voicing: Voiceless (vocal cords stay wide open and silent)
articulation.airflow: Oral, central sibilant groove with high-pressure burst (ʰ)

word_breakdown.note: Denti-alveolar stop closure released into a sharp sibilant with a strong puff of air.
Vertical vowel sign following छ that shifts the inherent vowel /ʌ/ to open /a/.
Tongue tip touches the back of the upper front teeth (marked by the under-bridge in /t̪/) with zero aspiration.
Ends the word on an open, relaxed /a/ vowel.

mouth_placement_steps: Place the tip and front blade of the tongue firmly against the denti-alveolar region (right behind the upper front teeth) to form an airtight seal.
Keep the vocal cords completely open and unvibrating while building air pressure behind the tongue closure.
Release the tongue tip slightly into a narrow front groove to produce a crisp '/t͡s/' ('ts' as in 'cats') fused with an immediate, forceful gust of breath ('ʰ').

coaching_game.title: The Paper Umbrella Puff Test
coaching_game.setup: Hold a lightweight strip of tissue paper (our 'paper umbrella') 2 inches in front of your child's lips.
coaching_game.action: Have your child say /t͡sʰ/ and then the full word छाता (/t͡sʰat̪a/).
coaching_game.success_cue: On the very first sound /t͡sʰ/, the tissue strip should visibly leap forward from the burst of air (ʰ), then stay completely still during the unaspirated second syllable /t̪a/!

common_pitfalls.issue: Using an English Postalveolar 'Ch' [t͡ʃ] Instead of Nepali Denti-Alveolar /t͡sʰ/
common_pitfalls.fix: Romanization writes छ as 'chha', tempting English speakers to use the 'ch' in 'church' ([t͡ʃ]). In Standard Nepali, the च-series is produced further forward at the teeth ridge with a 'ts' release (/t͡sʰ/). Cue the child with the end of 'cats' + a big puff of air!

common_pitfalls.issue: Dropping the Aspiration Burst (ʰ) and Merging छ (/t͡sʰ/) with च (/t͡s/)
common_pitfalls.fix: Nepali strictly contrasts unaspirated च (/t͡s/) and aspirated छ (/t͡sʰ/) (e.g., चार /t͡sar/ 'four' vs. छार /t͡sʰar/ 'ash'). Have the child feel a cool gust of wind on the back of their hand when pronouncing छ.

common_pitfalls.issue: Using an English Alveolar [tʰ] on the Second Syllable (/t̪a/)
common_pitfalls.fix: Watch the dental bridge in /t͡sʰat̪a/! For त (/t̪/), the tongue tip must touch the back of the upper front teeth with zero puff of air—saving all the wind for the opening छ (/t͡sʰ/).
